entries.position: both — but big meaning older (my big sister) only before a noun
entries.takes: on + noun or -ing (informal: very enthusiastic about); of + person in That's big of you
entries.contrast: Double the g: bigger, biggest, never biger. Big and large both mean большой, but large is more formal and goes with amount, number, quantity and sizes; only big means important (a big decision), older (my big brother) or popular (big in Japan), so a large mistake and my large brother are wrong. In think big and talk big, big is an adverb.

entries.contrast: Double the t: hotter, hottest. Russian splits heat in two, жаркий for weather and rooms and горячий for things you touch; English uses hot for both. I'm hot = мне жарко, never It's hot to me. Weather that is only pleasant is warm (тепло); hot is too much. Hot food can mean spicy (острый), so say spicy when you mean pepper. Hot about a person is informal and means sexy, so be careful with it.

entries.takes: of + noun (missing: wide of the goal)
entries.contrast: Drop the e and add -r: wider, widest. Russian широкий for shoulders or a general idea is usually broad: broad shoulders, in broad terms. In wide open and wide awake, wide is an adverb, and widely means by many people (widely known). The suffix -wide means across a whole area (nationwide).

examples: Is it true that you're moving to Denver?
The movie is based on a true story.
Nothing could be truer.
She's a true friend.
Nobody knew his true feelings.
Their dream finally came true.
He stayed true to his word.
The band has remained true to its roots.
Be true to yourself.
The painting is true to life.
A compass doesn't point to true north.
The same is true of most big cities.
That's especially true for older workers.

senses.head: Based on facts; not false
examples: Is it true that you're moving to Denver?
The movie is based on a true story.
Nothing could be truer.

senses.head: Real and genuine
examples: She's a true friend.
Nobody knew his true feelings.
Their dream finally came true.

senses.head: Loyal and faithful
examples: He stayed true to his word.
The band has remained true to its roots.
Be true to yourself.

senses.head: Accurate; exactly matching the real thing
examples: The painting is true to life.
A compass doesn't point to true north.

senses.head: Applying to someone or something
examples: The same is true of most big cities.
That's especially true for older workers.

entries.position: both — but true meaning real (a true friend) mostly before a noun
entries.takes: to + noun (loyal, faithful: true to his word); of or for + noun (applies to); that-clause (It's true that)
entries.contrast: Drop the e and add -r: truer, truest, but the adverb truly loses the e completely (not truely). Russian верно! or правда! as an answer is That's true or That's right; about a person, say You're right, never You're true. True of or true for means applies to (справедливо для): The same is true of cats.
